title: Stream segmentation and KV-slot throttling for low-jitter streaming completions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Streaming chat workloads show variable tail latency caused by large, heterogeneous sessions that monopolize KV cache slots and create GPU memory fragmentation. Existing continuous batcher coalesces turns aggressively which reduces throughput but increases jitter for interactive users when a single long session expands its KV footprint.

Goal: Implement a lightweight stream segmentation layer plus a KV-slot throttling policy to produce compact, low-jitter batches for streaming completions while preserving overall GPU utilization. The change should be conservative (feature-flagged) and observable via the Console.

Scope:
- Segmentation: detect long-running sessions and split them into "active segment" and "background segment" for batching decisions; maintain correct KV semantics (no model quality regression).
- KV-slot throttling: introduce per-session soft limits and a reclaim policy that avoids evicting live-turn KV entries mid-response; throttle expansion to a token-per-second budget and deprioritize background segments under pressure.
- GPU memory accounting: add a lightweight estimator to the batch planner to predict per-batch peak GPU footprint (prefix + KV) and prevent slab overcommit.
- Observability: expose metrics for segment counts, throttled expansions, predicted vs actual peak memory, and rejection/fallback events.

Non-goals: global rework of KV eviction strategies, cross-model remapping, or changing model weights/quantization in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Feature-flagged segmentation + KV-slot throttling can be enabled via runtime flag `seg_kv_throttle` without restarting nodes
End-to-end regression test harness shows <=5% quality delta on curated prompt set compared to baseline
Median tail jitter (95p latency variance measured as stddev across 10s windows) reduced by >=30% for interactive sessions in staging workload
GPU OOMs do not increase in stress test (10M tokens/hour staging harness); if a node hits OOM the system falls back to conservative batching and emits an incident metric
Console dashboard has new charts for segment distribution, throttled sessions, predicted vs actual batch GPU footprint, and KPI alerts wired
Documentation (runtime flags + Console widgets) merged and a short runbook published to Confluence

comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created. Attached rough latency plots from customer repro and staging traces. Proposed soft-limit rather than hard eviction to avoid mid-response KV misses.

2026-03-11 - Marco Delgado: Spiked a PoC that tags 'background segments' for sessions exceeding 8k tokens; early results show improved 95p latency but some increase in token cost. Need to quantify cost-quality tradeoff.

2026-03-12 - Eleni Markovic: KV soft-limit impl sketched: per-session token budget + backoff multiplier. Will avoid evicting any KV entry referenced by an in-flight stream. Questions about shared KV across model variants.

2026-03-12 - Rajiv: Planner estimator design v1 posted; uses prefix_length*kv_slot_size + predicted continuation tokens upper bound with 1.2 safety multiplier. Will integrate with the GPU slab tracker.
